candidate.title: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis
candidate.diseaseDescription: Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis: autoimmunity, endothelial injury, fibroblast activation and skin fibrosis, with interstitial lung disease and renal crisis branches. Mixed-subset SSc studies retain their context; excludes limited cutaneous disease, morphea and overlap syndromes.
candidate.releaseNote: Overall scientific summary of diffuse-systemic-sclerosis-summary-candidate-a3dc66504f57; external current-literature review remains pending. Overall scientific summary of diffuse-systemic-sclerosis-appraised-candidate-9ffacfbd27e3; external current-literature review remains pending. Provisional automatic appraisal of diffuse-systemic-sclerosis-therapy-candidate-20261017-001. Automatic conservative metadata appraisal. Source entailment, study quality, broad disease coverage, circuit causation and independent replication require review. Confidence is capped at 1/4 until explicit editorial appraisal; therapeutic categories describe curated target coverage, not efficacy. No calibration or human approval is asserted. Independent review and calibration remain pending.

entities.label: Anti-topoisomerase I antibodies
entities.description: ATA / Scl-70: autoantibodies used for phenotypic stratification; pathogenicity is not established by clinical association.

entities.label: Anti-RNA polymerase III antibodies
entities.description: ARA: autoantibodies associated with diffuse skin involvement and renal crisis; not a proven direct cause of these outcomes.

entities.label: SSc autoantibody immune complexes
entities.description: Experimentally precipitated serum immune complexes; autoantibody group and nucleic-acid cargo affect responses.

entities.label: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells
entities.description: Innate immune cells studied in SSc skin/blood and experimental systems.

entities.label: CXCL4 (platelet factor 4)
entities.description: Chemokine with a demonstrated capacity to organize DNA and amplify innate sensing.

entities.label: CXCL4–DNA complexes
entities.description: DNA assemblies formed with CXCL4; distinct from autoantibody immune complexes.

entities.label: Type I interferon signature
entities.description: IFN-I activity and IFN-alpha production in the indicated cell and patient systems.

entities.label: Effector CD8+ T cells
entities.description: Activated peripheral effector T cells with altered IL-13 production in selected SSc cohorts.

entities.label: IL-13
entities.description: Type 2 cytokine tested for fibroblast collagen induction.

entities.label: STAT6 signalling
entities.description: IL-13-associated signalling tested by inhibition and knockdown in dermal cultures.

entities.label: Macrophages
entities.description: Myeloid cells localized in early untreated dcSSc skin; ligand-receptor inference is retained as inference.

entities.label: Platelet-derived growth factor
entities.description: PDGF ligands involved in fibroblast signalling; isoforms and experimental exposure remain study-specific.

entities.label: Endothelial cells
entities.description: HUVECs in the immune-complex experiments; not an assumption of equivalent renal endothelial responses.

entities.label: Endothelin-1
entities.description: Vasoactive mediator measured in stimulated cultures.

entities.label: IL-6
entities.description: Cytokine studied through trans-signalling and trial-specific receptor blockade.

entities.label: JAK / STAT3 signalling
entities.description: IL-6 trans-signalling-associated pathway; no universal pathway sufficiency is asserted.

entities.label: TGF-beta
entities.description: Profibrotic growth-factor signalling; individual isoforms and perturbations remain explicit.

entities.label: SMAD3 signalling
entities.description: Downstream mediator in the IL-6 / TGF-beta culture model.

entities.label: Dermal fibroblasts
entities.description: Dermal mesenchymal cells across skin cultures and early dcSSc tissue observations.

entities.label: Myofibroblasts
entities.description: Activated contractile fibroblast phenotype; marker expression alone does not establish lineage.

entities.label: Collagen / extracellular-matrix deposition
entities.description: Matrix accumulation and experimentally measured collagen expression/release; these measurements are distinguished in evidence.

entities.label: Skin fibrosis
entities.description: Diffuse cutaneous thickening and skin fibrosis; modified Rodnan scores measure clinical involvement.

entities.label: Lung fibroblasts
entities.description: Cultures isolated from SSc-ILD lungs or controls; no assumption that skin and lung cell populations are identical.

entities.label: Interstitial lung disease
entities.description: SSc-associated fibrotic lung disease; mixed-cutaneous-subset studies retain their enrolled populations.

entities.label: Decline in lung function
entities.description: Forced vital capacity decline measured in SSc-ILD trials; distinct from reversal of established fibrosis.

entities.label: Renal arteriolar vasculopathy
entities.description: Biopsy arterial intimal thickening and arteriolar fibrinoid necrosis in renal crisis.

entities.label: Scleroderma renal crisis
entities.description: Acute renal vascular syndrome with kidney dysfunction and often severe hypertension.

entities.label: Acute kidney injury
entities.description: Acute renal failure and dialysis outcomes in renal-crisis cohorts.

entities.label: Severe hypertension
entities.description: Blood pressure elevation in renal crisis; normotensive presentations remain possible.

entities.label: Renin–angiotensin system
entities.description: Angiotensin-dependent blood pressure component inferred from physiology and ACE blockade; baseline renin does not reliably predict crisis.

entities.label: Severe dcSSc global outcome
entities.description: SCOT hierarchical composite of death, organ-failure-free survival, FVC, disability and skin score; not equivalent to isolated skin efficacy.

claims.text: In early dcSSc, ATA positivity was associated with more prevalent ILD than ARA positivity (69.6% versus 44.3%).
limitations: Observational subgroup comparison; neither necessary nor sufficient for ILD.

claims.text: ARA-positive early dcSSc participants had higher baseline skin scores than ATA-positive participants.
limitations: Association does not demonstrate antibody-mediated skin injury.

claims.text: ARA-positive early dcSSc participants had higher SRC prevalence than ATA-positive participants (14.4% versus 0%).
limitations: Phenotypic association; not proof of direct renal pathogenicity.

claims.text: The experimental SSc-IC preparations included material isolated from ATA-positive sera.
limitations: Preparation-level membership; does not isolate an antibody-specific causal effect.

claims.text: The experimental SSc-IC preparations included material isolated from ARA-positive sera.
limitations: Mixed cargo and very small specificity groups; ARA effects differ from ATA.

claims.text: SSc immune-complex preparations induced inflammatory signalling in healthy endothelial cultures.
limitations: Culture activation does not establish the initiating event or endothelial death in patients.

claims.text: IC-stimulated endothelial cultures increased IL-6 secretion.
limitations: In-vitro secretion, not a quantitative estimate of the in-vivo source.

claims.text: ATA-containing IC preparations increased endothelial endothelin-1 expression.
limitations: ET-1 mRNA response is not equivalent to measured vasoconstriction.

claims.text: ARA and ACA IC preparations did not upregulate ET-1, qualifying generalization across antibody groups.
limitations: Negative group-specific result; does not exclude other endothelial effects.

claims.text: ATA IC exposure increased endothelial TGF-beta1 secretion.
limitations: Selected full-text result; not a property of all specificities.

claims.text: ARA ICs did not significantly increase endothelial TGF-beta1 secretion.
limitations: Small ARA sample, retained as a qualification.

claims.text: Medium from SSc-IC-stimulated endothelial cells induced a profibrotic phenotype in skin fibroblasts.
limitations: Conditioned-medium experiment; not evidence of an obligatory complete in-vivo circuit.

claims.text: Endothelial conditioned medium increased TGF-beta1 secretion by fibroblasts.
limitations: Cell culture only.

claims.text: ATA-conditioned endothelial medium increased fibroblast COL1A1 expression.
limitations: Transcript outcome; does not alone prove matrix deposition in patients.

claims.text: ARA-conditioned medium did not significantly change fibroblast COL1A1 expression.
limitations: Specific assay and small groups; do not interpret ARA as nonfibrotic in patients.

claims.text: TGF-beta1 stimulation increased COL1A1 expression in cultured skin fibroblasts.
limitations: Expression is not a clinical fibrosis endpoint.

claims.text: Activated pDCs from the SSc study secreted CXCL4.
limitations: Mixed-subset SSc study; no assertion that all dcSSc patients share this pathway.

claims.text: Activated pDCs from the SSc study secreted IFN-alpha.
limitations: Cellular production; does not imply IFN blockade is an established therapy.

claims.text: CXCL4 organized DNA into complexes that amplify innate sensing.
limitations: Mixed-subset observations; DNA is a required component.

claims.text: CXCL4–DNA complexes amplified TLR9-mediated pDC activation in experiments.
limitations: TLR9-dependent activity; not dependent on CXCR3 in this system.

claims.text: Blood CXCL4–DNA complexes correlated with IFN-I activity in SSc.
limitations: Association is distinct from the functional assay and does not prove a universal clinical loop.

claims.text: Activated effector CD8 T cells from SSc patients produced increased IL-13.
limitations: Peripheral activation assay; tissue contribution and antigen specificity unresolved.

claims.text: Excess effector-CD8 IL-13 production correlated with skin fibrosis and was more pronounced in dcSSc.
limitations: Correlation does not establish IL-13 as the sole skin fibrosis driver.

claims.text: IL-13-induced collagen expression in dermal cultures depended on STAT6.
limitations: A compressed signalling edge; no clinical efficacy inference.

claims.text: STAT6 perturbation blocked IL-13-induced collagen expression.
limitations: This IL-13 route was TGF-beta1-independent, so it must not be drawn as obligatorily passing through TGF-beta.

claims.text: IL-6 trans-signalling-induced collagen expression in healthy dermal fibroblasts depended on STAT3.
limitations: Trans-signalling requires soluble receptor; not an unrestricted effect of IL-6 alone.

claims.text: STAT3-dependent IL-6 trans-signalling indirectly enhanced TGF-beta signalling through Gremlin-1.
limitations: Gremlin-1 is an omitted intermediate; a compressed mechanism, not a direct STAT3–TGF-beta interaction.

claims.text: The IL-6 trans-signalling culture mechanism involved enhanced TGF-beta signalling and SMAD3.
limitations: Context-specific downstream mechanism; not proof every fibrotic pathway requires SMAD3.

claims.text: SMAD3-mediated TGF-beta signalling contributed to IL-6 trans-signalling-induced collagen in cultures.
limitations: Intermediate Gremlin-1 retained in prose; not a whole-disease sufficiency claim.

claims.text: Macrophage PDGF expression and spatial proximity to receptor-high fibroblasts supported a proposed signalling niche.
limitations: Transcript and spatial inference do not prove secretion, direction or necessity in patients.

claims.text: Early dcSSc macrophage clusters expressed profibrotic factors including TGFB.
limitations: Selected full-text observation; ligand-receptor inference remains provisional.

claims.text: Reanalysis of PDGF-exposed SSc dermal fibroblasts supported PDGF-driven activation.
limitations: Culture response and tissue inference are separate; independent dataset reuse is not independent clinical replication.

claims.text: Dermal cultures exhibited growth-factor-associated myofibroblast differentiation that nintedanib reduced.
limitations: Culture phenotype; mouse antifibrotic findings do not establish human skin efficacy.

claims.text: TGF-beta blockade in an uncontrolled early dcSSc trial was accompanied by reduced dermal myofibroblast infiltration.
limitations: No placebo arm; temporal biomarker changes support involvement but do not establish clinical efficacy.

claims.text: Myofibroblast reduction and skin-score improvement occurred after fresolimumab in the same uncontrolled study.
limitations: Co-occurrence is not a mediation analysis; spontaneous skin improvement and small sample limit inference.

claims.text: TGF-beta-regulated matrix-related gene expression changes tracked skin-score changes in the fresolimumab study.
limitations: Bounded biomarker/clinical association; matrix gene changes do not prove removal of established collagen.

claims.text: PDGF stimulated proliferation of cultured lung fibroblasts from SSc-ILD patients.
limitations: Small culture study; not an estimate of clinical disease contribution.

claims.text: PDGF-induced normal lung fibroblast differentiation into myofibroblasts was blocked by nintedanib.
limitations: Do not transfer the normal-cell differentiation assay to every diseased lung fibroblast.

claims.text: Nintedanib reduced collagen and fibronectin production in lung-fibroblast experiments.
limitations: Production in cultures is distinct from reversal of established lung fibrosis.

claims.text: SENSCIS enrolled SSc-ILD patients with at least 10% lung fibrosis on HRCT.
limitations: Eligibility linkage; not a new mechanistic causal finding or universal fibrosis threshold.

claims.text: SSc-ILD participants experienced FVC decline, slower with nintedanib than placebo in the primary SENSCIS analysis.
limitations: Association edge describes the phenotype/outcome; drug efficacy is represented separately.

claims.text: SRC biopsies showed arterial intimal thickening and arteriolar fibrinoid necrosis associated with poor renal outcome.
limitations: Biopsy association; does not establish the vascular initiation sequence.

claims.text: Acute biopsy vascular changes in SRC were associated with poorer renal outcomes.
limitations: Selected biopsies; direction and confounding cannot be resolved from this series.

claims.text: SRC was associated with acute renal failure and temporary or permanent dialysis.
limitations: Clinical phenotype; the association does not identify a molecular cause.

claims.text: SRC usually presented with hypertension; lower presenting pressure was associated with poor renal outcome.
limitations: Normotensive SRC remains possible; severe hypertension is not required in every case.

claims.text: Successful captopril blood-pressure control in four SRC patients supported an angiotensin-dependent component.
limitations: Pharmacological inference; no direct proof that RAAS initiates the full renal-crisis pathway.

claims.text: Reduced renal plasma flow and elevated renin activity were common in a physiological SSc cohort.
limitations: Mixed-subset cohort; not a direct renal-ischaemia-to-renin experiment.

claims.text: Isolated reduced plasma flow or elevated renin did not predict SRC.
limitations: Retained negative finding; no baseline-renin prediction claim.

claims.text: SENSCIS primary analysis found slower annual FVC decline with nintedanib (difference 41.0 mL/year, 95% CI 2.9–79.0).
limitations: 576 treated; 51.9% diffuse cutaneous; lung-function slowing is not fibrosis reversal.

claims.text: SENSCIS multiple-imputation sensitivity analyses gave P values of 0.06–0.10, qualifying the positive primary result.
limitations: Sensitivity to handling missing data; no mortality benefit asserted.

claims.text: SENSCIS did not show a significant skin-score benefit (difference -0.21, 95% CI -0.94 to 0.53).
limitations: Secondary outcome, no human skin efficacy inferred from preclinical antifibrotic activity.

claims.text: Nintedanib inhibited proliferation and migration of SSc-ILD lung fibroblasts in culture.
limitations: Fibroblasts are an indirect cellular target; direct targets are kinases, not PDGF ligand.

claims.text: focuSSced secondary FVC findings favoured tocilizumab (4.2 percentage-point difference, nominal analysis).
limitations: Primary skin endpoint failed; selected early inflammatory dcSSc; two linked correction notices could not be fully inspected. Current US label independently confirms SSc-ILD indication.

Current US label independently confirms overall-population ppFVC difference 4.20; 2021 correction changes SSc-ILD subgroup TCZ mean to 0.1. Journal-versus-label randomized denominator differs (210 versus 212), not reconciled.

claims.text: focuSSced did not meet the primary skin fibrosis endpoint (adjusted difference -1.73, 95% CI -3.78 to 0.32; P=0.10).
limitations: No demonstrated primary skin benefit; original trial correction details remain pending.

claims.text: Tocilizumab inhibits IL-6 signalling by binding IL-6 receptors.
limitations: IL-6 is an indirect mapped target; receptor is not separately represented.

claims.text: In SLS II, MMF recipients had improved FVC percent predicted from baseline to 24 months (+2.19 points).
limitations: Within-arm improvement; no placebo arm; does not prove superiority or equivalence to cyclophosphamide.

claims.text: In SLS II, cyclophosphamide recipients had improved FVC percent predicted from baseline to 24 months (+2.88 points).
limitations: Within-arm improvement; toxicity and withdrawal differed; no assertion of equal efficacy.

claims.text: SLS II did not confirm the hypothesised MMF superiority over cyclophosphamide (primary analysis P=0.24).
limitations: 142 randomized, 126 in primary analysis; negative superiority result is not equivalence.

claims.text: Cyclophosphamide caused more leukopenia and premature treatment withdrawal than MMF in SLS II.
limitations: Harms qualify therapeutic use; this is not an endpoint-specific efficacy contradiction.

claims.text: The historical SRC cohort had higher one-year survival in the ACE-inhibitor era (76% versus 15%).
limitations: Nonrandomized historical comparison; secular confounding; use at established SRC is distinct from prophylaxis.

claims.text: Captopril controlled blood pressure in a four-patient SRC case series.
limitations: Small uncontrolled series; inhibition of the renin–angiotensin pathway is mapped, ACE itself is not a separate node.

claims.text: SCOT favoured myeloablative autologous HSCT over monthly cyclophosphamide on the 54-month global rank composite (P=0.01).
limitations: 75 selected severe scleroderma participants; comparator is cyclophosphamide, not all current treatments.

claims.text: SCOT transplant treatment-related mortality was 3% at 54 months and 6% at 72 months, versus 0% with cyclophosphamide.
limitations: Treatment selection and cardiopulmonary screening are essential; not generalizable to advanced cardiorespiratory involvement.

therapies.name: Nintedanib
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits receptor tyrosine kinases including PDGFR, FGFR and VEGFR; mapped fibroblast effects are indirect.
therapies.indication: US: slowing pulmonary-function decline in adults with SSc-ILD. No skin indication asserted.
therapies.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
therapies.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Diarrhoea was frequent; not a fibrosis cure or proven skin treatment.

therapies.name: Tocilizumab
therapies.mechanismOfAction: IL-6 receptor blockade inhibits downstream IL-6 signalling; IL-6 ligand is an indirect target.
therapies.indication: US: slowing pulmonary-function decline in adults with SSc-ILD; subcutaneous use. No general dcSSc skin approval asserted.
therapies.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
therapies.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Trial secondary lung result; primary skin endpoint negative; original correction notices remain incompletely resolved.

therapies.name: Mycophenolate mofetil
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Immunosuppressive treatment; the mapped clinical lung-function outcome is an indirect effect, not a direct molecular target.
therapies.indication: Guideline-supported SSc-ILD use; trial duration and tolerability apply. No SSc-specific approval asserted.
therapies.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
therapies.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Guideline-supported use. The schema has no off-label category: unverified denotes no SSc-specific regulatory approval verified here, not experimental clinical practice.
Direct IMPDH target and immune-cell mechanisms are not separately curated.

therapies.name: Cyclophosphamide
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Broad immunosuppression; clinical lung-function effects are indirect, not direct target binding.
therapies.indication: Guideline-supported SSc-ILD; toxicity constrains treatment. No SSc-specific approval asserted.
therapies.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
therapies.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Guideline-supported use. The schema has no off-label category: unverified denotes no SSc-specific regulatory approval verified here, not experimental clinical practice.
Not a preferred treatment recommendation or universal disease reversal claim.

therapies.name: ACE inhibitors (captopril representative)
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme and reduces angiotensin signalling; RAAS is an indirect pathway target.
therapies.indication: EULAR: use immediately at diagnosis of SRC. This record does not endorse prophylactic use.
therapies.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
therapies.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Guideline-supported use. The schema has no off-label category: unverified denotes no SSc-specific regulatory approval verified here, not experimental clinical practice.
Renal recovery is variable; survival evidence is primarily historical observational.

therapies.name: Autologous haematopoietic stem-cell transplantation
therapies.modality: Myeloablative immunosuppression and autologous stem-cell rescue
therapies.mechanismOfAction: High-intensity immunosuppression followed by stem-cell rescue; global disease outcome is an indirect clinical effect, not a molecular target.
therapies.indication: EULAR: selected early severe dcSSc with poor prognosis, without advanced cardiorespiratory involvement.
therapies.jurisdiction: United States approvals where explicitly verified; EULAR guidance separately labelled
therapies.trialPhase: Completed clinical study; population and endpoints restricted as described
limitations: Procedure status is not equivalent to a drug indication; no regulatory approval claimed.
Treatment-related mortality and strict specialist selection apply.
